note: Bluusun Decision API, model id bluusun/decision-1 (production endpoint https://www.bluusun.com/api/v1/decide). Per the author: a frozen Qwen 3.7 Max first-token logit readout restricted to the option letters (temperature 0, reasoning off, renormalised over the caller's options); the output is never model text. Documented limits: 2-16 options, evidence capped at 3,000 characters (longer requests are refused unbilled). Measured through a minimal reviewed stdlib loopback shim (w2d/worker/bluusun_shim.py) that maps JevBench's TypeSafe request onto the author's documented native request unchanged (evidence = state, criterion = instructions, options = the declared options with their descriptions, in request order) and passes the returned probabilities through without renormalisation; the API's documented 3,000-character refusal is counted as a wrong answer (422), as in the length-limited GPU rows. Closed weights and training data: training-data overlap with the 231 public items is UNVERIFIED (the author states no training on JevBench or openjev). The author's openjev numbers (0.956) are his own claim, not a JevBench number. Evaluation key: prepaid test credit supplied by the author.
note_v14: Hosted-API measurement of all 842 decisions (534 frozen v1.2 + 308 sealed v1.4), sent one at a time from Sandy (Hetzner, Germany) through JevBench's unchanged typesafe adapter and the reviewed loopback shim to the operator's production endpoint; the endpoint received sealed item text, never answers or labels. Latency is the serial client wall time (network included) on the standard+judge items, unadjusted as for every production API row. Cost is the operator's public bookable list price, a flat $0.005 per decision (www.bluusun.com pricing, credit packs via Stripe; snapshot in receipts/), i.e. $5.00 per 1,000 decisions.
